Prevention: Harvest nearby alfalfa, vetch or clover before winged adults are formed in the spring as pea aphids overwinter as eggs on leaves and stems of perennial legumes.
Liberal nitrogen applications increase aphid populations.
Avoid excessive use of nitrogen fertlizers, i.e. not more than 20-25 kg.
Among abiotic factors, rain and wind can dramatically reduce aphid infestations.

Promote natural enemies presence such as lady beetles, big-eyed bugs, damsel bugs, minute pirate bugs and syrphid flies by reducing pesticide applications and providing natural habitat to the predators.
Monitoring: Start monitoring when plants begin to flower.
Action threshold includes (plant height to pea aphids); Under 10"- 40 to 50 aphids per stem; 10 to 20" - 70 to 80 aphids per stem ; over 20" 100 + aphids per stem.
Stem samples give useful estimates of aphid density.
Pea aphids are common in spring, but also active in autumn and winter.
To check the population dynamics, place yellow containers full of water near peas.
They may also attract and trap the pea aphids before they can harm the plants.
Infestations during bloom and early pod stages will reduce yield and crop quality by impairing pod appearance, reducing seed fill and by the presence of aphid honey- dew.
Direct Control: Rake up all fallen plant material after harvest to prevent aphids from overwintering in your field.
Restrictions: Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants and long-sleeve shirts whilst spraying.
Change clothes and wash your hands immediately after applying pesticides.
Don't spray outdoors on windy or rainy days.
